nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Red flowers on white stone. It's beautiful. It shouldn't be here.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: This is where a piece of the Manalith came down and took root. It's not only death up there. That's the strangest thing I've seen.

nodes.speaker: class-hierarch
nodes.line: Thieves from the holds, in my own white wagon. Do you know how long I have kept the Manalith in the sky?

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The Anchors hold the Manalith. They need a thread of the tithe. You drank everything else.

nodes.speaker: class-hierarch
nodes.line: Two hundred years of it, and I am still here. While my Choir sings, I do not stay down.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Silence the Choir first. Everything every hold ever paid is in that organ. Let's give it back!

payload.title: The Keeper of the Great Anchor

nodes.speaker: class-cyclops02
nodes.line: Small. Warm. Loud. Keeper holds the big arch. Keeper was grown to hold it. You are not allowed.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Grown? In a white tank, out of somebody's tithe. Maybe somebody from Saltmoss.

nodes.speaker: class-cyclops02
nodes.line: Keeper does not remember. Keeper lifts a foot. Keeper stamps. Small things slide close to Keeper.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: When it lifts its foot, get clear, or stand ready. Whoever it drags in starts the first pincer.

payload.title: The Kiln Guard on the Stair

nodes.speaker: class-ceramicknight06
nodes.line: None climb to the cathedral. I was fired in the kiln for this stair. Side blows only scratch my glaze.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Then we come at you top to bottom, and keep cracking until the porcelain gives.

nodes.speaker: class-mechaarmor01
nodes.line: CHOIR DIG. TITHED CREWS ONLY. TURN BACK. ...Look, kids, I just drive this thing for the Red Seal. Go home.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Look at the crates, they're glowing. They're digging mana out of the Manalith's fallen shell.

nodes.speaker: class-mechaarmor01
nodes.line: SHIELD WALL ACTIVE. SIDE ASSAULTS WILL BE DEFLECTED. ...That's the card talking. The card's not wrong.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Side hits glance off that shield. Pincer it top to bottom, or keep cracking it until it breaks.

nodes.speaker: class-captain
nodes.line: Saltmoss runaways in a Choir wagon. I wear their white for the holds' sake, and you've made a fool of me.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You stood there while they took the colour out of your own people. Don't call us thieves.

nodes.speaker: class-captain
nodes.line: I kept the tithe at quota. Without me it's three times that. Give me room on my field and I strike twice.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Then no room. Stay close to the Captain, everyone. Never let the Captain end a turn alone.

nodes.speaker: class-oni02
nodes.line: The pass takes a toll. Leave the white wagon. This mask has fallen before. It always gets back up.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Then we cut down its raiders first. With no one left standing beside it, that mask stays down.

nodes.speaker: class-chronomancer
nodes.line: Mind the floor. You came to see the tithe? Look in tank nine. That's a whole hold, kept cold.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Roofs. A well. People, asleep. ...The Hollow aren't empty, are they? They're in there.

nodes.speaker: class-chronomancer
nodes.line: Not empty. Stored. The Anchors sip, the spire drinks, and I keep the clocks. Give me room and I take two turns.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Then no room. Close in on her, everyone. Someone stays beside her, every turn.

nodes.speaker: class-swampmistress00
nodes.line: Little drivers. This hull is mine. Halcyon built her to run from the sky, and the tide threw her here instead. The fen and I keep her now.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: It's a wreck in a swamp. Nobody's flying anything. You could walk away.

nodes.speaker: class-swampmistress00
nodes.line: And leave her to the Choir's salvage crews? My coven holds the mire for me. Strike at me and I'm simply... somewhere else.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: She trades places with her coven. Cut them down first, and she has nowhere left to go.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Back again? Mind the trays. The dust on them still remembers being part of something bigger.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Crust off the Manalith. Most of it's dead stone. A little still holds mana, and if you sing to it right, it gathers into a Shard instead of drifting home.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Not their Lullaby. I sang that for the Choir until I saw where the surplus went. Now I only hum to the trays. They listen better.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Go carefully. And bring me anything that glitters when the Manalith is up.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Back with more scrapes? Sit. Don't touch the green bottle.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Something that cures what the Shardfall does to blood. Mostly. Ask me again next week.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Drink water. Avoid the red rivers. Come back alive.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Gear holding up? Show me.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Halcyon steel, off the walkers at the dig. Twelve hundred years old and still better than anything I can make. Humbling.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Keep your edge clean.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: The runes are restless tonight. So am I.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: That the Manalith is closer than it was last month. They always say that. They're always right.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Sleep well. I'll keep watch.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: There's soup on, and it's mostly vegetables. Mostly.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The Captain's still looking for us. Someone in the last hold swore they saw the Manalith blink. People talk.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Don't let it get cold.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: What'll it be? Gossip's free, the rest isn't. A sellsword's contract runs three hundred gold.

choices.text: About that map I sold you.
About what I said on the road.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Still accurate, mostly. The roads move when the Manalith pulls. Trust the lanterns over the paper.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Water under the bridge. I've been called worse by better customers.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Paid, signed, sealed. One sellsword, as promised. Treat them well and they'll stay.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Come back when your purse is heavier.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Got a moment?

choices.text: What do you make of the merchant?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Tired. Sore. Still here. That counts for something.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Sells us oil and sells us gossip. I trust the oil.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You too. Somebody has to keep the fire going.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Listen. That music. It's coming from the walls.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: It's the organ. It's full of everything every hold ever paid. The Hierarch drinks from it. Let's make it stop.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: There's something under the arches. Older stone.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Older than Halcyon. Whoever built this first knew exactly what they were holding in the sky.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: These arches go on forever. What are they holding up?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Nothing. They're not holding anything up. They're drawing something down. Feel the hum? That's where the light goes.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Halt. That's a Choir wagon on Anchor ice. Give me one reason my hammer stays on my back.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Because we stole it. We ran from the tithe at Saltmoss, and we're following the beams.

choices.text: Help us see where they go.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Worse than this? My hold sent me to guard these arches. Every night they hum, and our tithe rides the beam.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Saltmoss paid the same tithe as my hold. My shield is yours. I stand in front. It's what I'm for.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The Underspire's lights are brighter than ever.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: They're still drawing off Halcyon's old taps. Now the spire's empty, everyone wants it. Including the people pulling the Manalith closer.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Halcyon. It's so quiet. Where did everyone go?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Into the Manalith, the night it woke. And the Choir has been taking from us ever since. I say we give it back.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Sit down. You brought the Still's cold out with you. I can see it on your skin.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You're far off the Lantern Road. What brings a sage under the spire?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: I counted the pilgrims who climbed that stair. None came down. I'd rather climb with people who mean to.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then I'll mend you on the way up. Whatever drinks at the top of that spire, it has drunk enough.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The Ember are marching north. All of them.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: To the Anchors. They want to open every tap and drag the Manalith down. We can't let them reach the arches.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Don't step on the trays! Every grain on them took me a day to sift out of the sand.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You're sifting the Shardfall? The Choir punishes anyone who steals from its dig.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Then it's a good thing I'm leaving. You have a wagon and I have a trade: bring me dust, I'll make you Shards. Room for one more?

choices.text: Climb on. We could use a trade.
How do you make Shards out of dust?

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: I sing to it. I learned the Lullaby in the Cathedral's lower choir, then learned to sing it backwards. It makes the mana gather instead of drain.

nodes.speaker: character-aetherist
nodes.line: Then I'll set my trays by your fire. Keep bringing me dust and I'll keep you in Shards.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Careful where you step. I've got a whole batch drying on those rocks.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: A splice-cutter? Out here?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Someone has to study what the red rivers do. I could use a wagon. Mind if I come along?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Safer than leaving me here. I'll keep you patched up.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Here, take this bottle. You'll need it sooner than you think.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: See this? Shardfall sand, fired with a sliver of shell. It comes out as glass, and the glass remembers the heat. It remembers anything you pour through it.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Can it remember an edge? We're losing blades faster than we find them.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Give me a crucible and a few quiet nights at camp. Bring me shards and steel, and I'll find out what they'll take.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The whole desert's covered in spikes. Did they grow here?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Some fell. Some are stone. And some, I think, are the Manalith's own body, shed like old skin. Don't lick any.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Hey! White wagon! Don't run me down, I'm not with the Choir. I just look this dusty.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You're a long way from the Underspire. What are you doing out in the red?

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Rough? The Choir's dig hired me to fix their walkers, then stiffed me. They're cracking the Manalith's fallen shell open out there.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Deal. I'll fix your axle on the move. And keep the wagon moving. The Ember hates anything white.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The holds look different. Walls everywhere.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Without the Choir, nobody pays the tithe, so everyone's building walls. Funny how the rain always missed the rich holds.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You're the innkeeper from Saltmoss. You followed us?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Somebody had to. You stole the tithe wagon with no food and no plan.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: I'll cook, you fight. Fair?

choices.text: How much will it cost us?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Less than starving. Feed me and I'll feed you.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Good. Now, who's peeling the potatoes?

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: The Tithe Moors. Every hold's already paid, and the white wagons are still coming.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Three times the quota this year. Three times. Nobody's saying why, but everyone's looking up.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Easy, I'm not with the Choir. I followed the smoke from Saltmoss. You're the ones who stole their white wagon?

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: We are, and they'll want it back. Three of us against the whole moor. We could use a fourth.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Safe is the tithe line. I watched my aunt walk out of one white as chalk. I'll take the moor.

nodes.speaker: $recruit
nodes.line: Then I'm in. In the fens we know what the tithe really takes, and how to make it burn back.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: A white wagon with no white collectors on it. Now there's something you don't see.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: We're not Choir. Are you going to tell anyone?

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Not if you let me ride along. I've got lanterns, oil, and a very good map for twenty gold.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Sold. And a potion for good faith. Now, about that ride?

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Rude. I'm coming anyway. You'll need me.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Splendid. I'll set up shop in the back.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: That's a Choir wagon. And you're not Choir.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: You noticed. Are you going to turn us in?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: The Choir asked me to forge their tithe chains. I said no. I'll fix your gear if you take me with you.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Hand me your worst blade. There. Sharper than when you bought it.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Let's go before the Captain hears I'm missing.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: We've come a long way from Saltmoss. Can I ask you something?

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Ask.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Why did we run? Not the plan. The reason.

choices.text: For the coin on that wagon.
For the people the tithe would have hollowed.
To find out what the Choir's hiding.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Honest, at least. Coin buys food. I won't judge.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: That's what I hoped you'd say. That's why I came.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Something's wrong up there. I feel it too.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: We're a family now. A strange one, but a family.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Whatever the reason, we keep going.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Every shrine on this road has a board, and every board has names on it. Beasts, bandits, a deserter or two from the Red Seal.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: And somebody pays for those names?

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The shrines do, and the villages, when the Choir won't. I'll copy the board for camp. Bring back proof and I'll bring back coin.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: So many lanterns on the stairs. Who keeps them lit?

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: The pilgrims. Every one they light is a prayer the Manalith stays asleep. I sell the oil. Business is very good.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: There's a ring burned into the shrine floor, and every lantern on the wall leans toward it.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: A calling circle. Pilgrims used them to send for help along the road. Put coin in the bowl, and someone out there looking for a cause hears it.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Then we'll carry it back to camp. We need every hand we can get.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: It fills the whole sky. I can count the crystals.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: And the Moon's still there beside it, small and steady. Whatever we decide, we decide here.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Those cogs. Nobody cut those teeth. They grew.

nodes.speaker: $lead
nodes.line: Grew? Out of what?

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Out of whatever the gremlins drink at the dig. The Manalith's shell, maybe. I'll keep studying them.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: The Shardfall scorpions drink from the red rivers, and their venom changes faster than I can brew. Put down four so I can study a fresh batch?

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Four. Bring me the stingers while they're still warm.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Then watch your ankles out there.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The Bulwark march in white armour like they own Halcyon's streets. Six of them broken would make the Choir think twice about following us.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Six white shells. Let's go crack some.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Fine. But they'll keep coming.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The Cathedral's ahead, and the Choir won't go easy on us. I don't think we're strong enough yet. Let's get there before we climb.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Good. We go up when we're ready, not before.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: If you say so. I'll be right behind you.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Halcyon's ghosts are what's left of people tithed past Hollow. Just the shape of someone. Somebody should lay them to rest.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Five of them. Gently, if we can.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Maybe they're used to waiting.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: The ice maulers drink what leaks from the arches, and their cores never warm. Break three and bring me what's inside.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Three cold hearts. I want to know what keeps them cold.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: They'll still be out there.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Steel quenched in frost-core holds an edge forever. Two frost cores from the Wastes, and I'll show you.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Two cores. Keep them wrapped, or they'll freeze your hands.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Suit yourselves. Dull blades it is.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: This forge is cold, and I can't fix your gear with nothing. Six iron ore from the Shardfall would get the fire going.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Six. Pick the red-veined ones, they melt cleaner.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Then don't break anything.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: The walkers out at the dig are plated with Halcyon steel. Three plates off the wrecks and I can make armour worth wearing.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Three plates. Mind the wires.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Your armour, your problem.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The holds that used to pay the Captain's tithe have soldiers of their own now, and no masters. Ten of them still think they serve the Choir. Show them otherwise.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Ten. Remind them who they were before the tithe.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: They'll figure it out eventually.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: The moor frogs glow brighter on the nights the Manalith stirs. I think it's caught in their glands. Bring me three and I'll prove it.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Three glands. Don't squeeze them on the way back.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: It is slimy. That's science.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: The gremlins at the dig carry cogs with teeth no file ever cut. Bring me four. I want to know who's making them.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Four cogs. Something grew those, and I want to know what.

nodes.speaker: character-blacksmith
nodes.line: Then I'll keep guessing.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: The fen hags were Choir once. Now they sing mana into curses and bind them into their own claws. Three claws, and I might learn how they hold.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Three. Don't let them sing at you.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: It is grim. That's why I want to understand it.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The Bloom grows trees where nothing should grow. Their heartwood burns warm for days. Three pieces would keep this camp alive through anything.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Three. The red-grained kind, if you can.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: We'll manage with what we have.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: The Choir taught that a hymn needs every voice. I want to believe it can mean something kinder. Clear the heart of the Arkgrave with no one falling.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Every voice, then. I'll be watching.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: It is. That's what makes it worth asking.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: The Still's tanks are full of tithe, and some of it's turned holy. Three vials of holy mana and I can brew something that brings people back.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Three vials. Hold them gently, they remember who they were.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Then I'll wait.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: The Choir's Cantors lead the hymn that sings the holds into the Still's tanks. I know their parts by heart. Silence three, and I'll believe it can stop.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Three voices. Let's see what the quiet sounds like.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Then the hymn goes on.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The Cathedral will hurt us more than anywhere yet. Learn to mend the whole party at once before we climb, and we'll all come back down.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Good. I'd rather we all come home.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I hope you're right.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The cold off the Anchors gets into the beds. Three yeti furs would line the bunks before somebody wakes up blue.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Three. Big ones.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Fine, but you're sleeping on the edge.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: The swamp lurkers bleed something that knits wounds shut. Four vials and I can make charms that pull you back from the edge.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Four. Cork them tight.

nodes.speaker: character-alchemist
nodes.line: Gross saves lives.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Oni road-raiders are robbing pilgrims on the Lantern Road's stairs. Drive off three so the road's safe to trade on again.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: Three masks. Pilgrims will thank you, and so will my purse.

nodes.speaker: character-merchant
nodes.line: It's everyone's problem when trade stops.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: There's a spell that pulls a burning stone down from the sky. Learn it, and I'll stop worrying about what we meet next.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Good. Aim it away from the camp.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Dangerous is the point.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Harpies are nesting over the wells and stealing anything shiny. Four of them gone, and the water carriers can breathe again.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Four. Mind your rings.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Then keep your shiny things close.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Something's living in the cellar, and it's eating the cheese. Six slimes, at least. I'd go myself, but I like my boots.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Six. And save the cheese if you can.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: The cheese will not survive.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Something howls on the moors at night, and it isn't a wolf. Bring it down before it comes for the inn.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: One beast. Don't go alone.

nodes.speaker: character-innkeeper
nodes.line: Then lock the doors.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: The Choir's Confessors keep the hymn going under the organ. Silence three, and the pipes the Hierarch drinks from start to falter.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Three. Let's take that reservoir away.

nodes.speaker: character-enchantress
nodes.line: Then the Hierarch keeps drinking.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The reapers in Halcyon wear shrouds cut from something old. Two of them would tell us what the Choir is hiding up there.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Two shrouds. Don't wear them.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We'll learn some other way.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: I watched the Ronin fight. There's a guard stance in that style worth learning. Teach it, and the rest of us will rest easier.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Good. A blade that guards is worth two that swing.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Don't wait too long.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The Ronin has the makings of something great, but needs seasoning. Bring them up a little and they'll carry us.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Good. A little blood, a lot of practice.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: They'll get there.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: There's a ronin out on the moors. No lord, no school, good with a blade. If we found them, they might come with us.

nodes.speaker: $with

The enemy, if they stand close.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Yes. One call and the whole line wakes. Some habits survive twelve centuries.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Reveille isn't for me. It wakes everyone linked with me. Keep the line together.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Field Aid heals whoever I back. How close must I stay?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Two links. Quick in, quick out.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Field aid is short range. Two links, no more.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: White Mend heals whoever's striking. Where do I do the most good?

choices.text: Within three links of the ones fighting.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Good. Three links, and the light reaches.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: The light only reaches three links. Stay near the fight.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Wild Growth gives the ally I back regrowth. Who needs it?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Right. Growth takes time, so give it to the stayers.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Growth is slow, but it lasts. Give it to whoever stays in.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Flash Powder can blind what my ally strikes. Who's it for?

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Yes. Blind the big hitter and they swing at air.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Save the flash for the one who hurts most.

payload.title: A templar with a red sword

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You saw the red in my blade. Most people run when they see it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We've seen worse on this road. What is the red?

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Mana, taken too fast. I drank from the Shardfall to win a fight I was losing. Do you judge me?

choices.text: No. You did what you had to. What matters is what you do now.
I don't know enough to judge.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Sometimes the red wants more. If I start to lose myself, what will you do?

choices.text: Stand beside you until you find your way back.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Why fight at all? The Manalith comes either way.

choices.text: Because there's nothing else to do.
Because the people under it are worth fighting for.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The red is quiet. Strange. Let me listen to it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then I'll carry my red sword beside you. Point it at the right things.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No. The red says no. Better that I walk alone.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Hah! You fight hot. Good. The Shardfall has no respect for the cold.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: You fight like you're angry at the sky.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I am. Look at it, bigger every year. What should be done about the Manalith?

choices.text: Nothing. The Choir has it handled.
Something. Anything but sitting under it, singing.
I don't know yet. I'm still learning what it is.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: We drink from the red rivers out here. It burns. Would you?

choices.text: If it kept me fighting, yes.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The Choir digs up the Manalith's shell and sells it back to us. What would you do about their dig?

choices.text: Take it over and run it ourselves.
Shut it down and give the shards to the people they took them from.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let the fire settle. Then I'll know.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You'll do. I'll bring the heat, you bring the plan.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Bah. You're too cold for the Ember. Go on, then.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You fight well for people who don't know what they're bleeding.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Mana. Same as everyone. Same as you.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Good. Most don't even know the word. Do you know where the Choir sends the tithe?

choices.text: Up the spire to the Cathedral, and more of it than the Lullaby needs.
Somewhere it does good, I'm sure.
Up to the Manalith, to keep it asleep.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A healer spends a little of their own colour to mend you. Would you let them?

choices.text: Only if they'd let me do the same for them.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: I ran from the Choir. If they come for me, will you hand me over?

choices.text: I'd try to talk them out of it.
Never. Anyone who comes for you comes through us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Mm. The fen teaches us to listen twice.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then I'll come. Someone has to teach you what the colour costs.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No. I've run from one choir already. I won't join another.

payload.title: A sworn sword of the Holds

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Well fought. You held the line like you'd sworn to it.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We swore to each other. That's enough for us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: My hold paid the tithe every year and hated every drop. What did you do on tithe day?

choices.text: We kept our heads down and got out.
We stole the Choir's caravan, so Saltmoss kept its colour.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: An oath is only worth what it costs you. Would you keep one that hurt?

choices.text: Yes. That's the only kind that means anything.
Depends who I swore it to.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The Captain sold our tithe to the Choir. If you had the Captain at sword's point, what then?

choices.text: Walk away. It's not my fight.
Bring the Captain back to answer to the holds.
Strike a deal. The Captain pays well.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Give me a moment. I don't swear lightly.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then I swear it: my sword is yours until the road ends. Lead on.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No. You haven't earned an oath from me. Go with care.

payload.title: A walker of the Lantern Road

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The lanterns burned brighter while you fought. The monks would call that a good sign.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We could use a few good signs.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A pilgrim walks the road without asking where it ends. Why do you walk it?

choices.text: To find out everything the monks are hiding.
To keep moving. Every step is one the Choir didn't take from us.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Who keeps the lanterns lit?

choices.text: Whoever walks past an empty one.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A student is only as good as the master. Who taught you to fight?

choices.text: Everyone who has stood beside me, and everyone I've lost.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let me sit with your answers, the way the masters taught.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Then I'll walk your road. We'll keep the lanterns lit together.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No. Our roads part here. May the lanterns light yours.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You fought well. Better than the beasts, anyway. I've been walking this road alone a long time.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: So did you. We could use someone who doesn't run.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Tell me straight. Why are you out here in a stolen Choir wagon?

choices.text: Because the tithe was taking people we love, and somebody had to stop paying.
We needed a way out, and the wagon was there.
For the loot. That wagon was full.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The Manalith is bigger every season. What do you think it is?

choices.text: A rock in the sky. I try not to look at it.
Whatever the Choir says it is.
Nobody knows. Anyone who says they do is selling something.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: If I come with you, what do I get?

choices.text: A share of everything, and people who'll stand beside you.
Food, a fire and a fight most days.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Hm. Let me think on that.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: All right. I'll walk with you for a while. Don't make me regret it.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: No. Not this road, not yet. Maybe we'll meet again.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Nice work. You fight like Underspire kids, all elbows and no manners.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: Some of us are. You're a long way from the neon.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Out here you're the ones in the Choir's white wagon. So which is it: collectors or runners?

choices.text: Just travellers. The paint came with it.
Runners. We took the wagon so the tithe never got where it was going.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Underspire rule one. What do you do when the Red Seal comes down your street?

choices.text: Split up, take the roofs, meet at the noodle stall later.
Stand there and pay. It's easier.
Hide and hope they pick another door.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The whole Underspire runs its lights off Halcyon's old taps. Should we shut them off?

choices.text: That's for someone smarter than me.
Not on our own. But we should know what they're pulling on.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let me count what you said against what you did out there.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: You're all right. I'll run with your crew. Somebody has to watch your backs.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Nah. You talk like you've never been squeezed. Catch you around.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: The beasts here listen to me. They didn't mind you. That's rare.

nodes.speaker: $with
nodes.line: We didn't come to hurt anything that leaves us alone.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Out in the Bloom, red things grow where pieces of the Manalith fell. Should we burn them?

choices.text: No. Something growing isn't the same as something hurting.
Burn it all. It came from the sky.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: A wolf takes a sheep from a hold. Who's wrong?

choices.text: The wolf. Hunt down every one.
Nobody. The wolf is hungry and the hold is poor. Fix the hunger.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: If I come, my animals come too. Will your people mind fur in the stew?

choices.text: Bring them. A camp with beasts in it is never taken by surprise.
Leave them. They'll slow us down.
As long as they don't eat the rations.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: Let me ask them what they think. ...They're thinking.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: They like you. So do I, a little. We'll come.

nodes.speaker: $hero
nodes.line: They don't trust you. Neither do I. Off you go.
